_note: Reporter wordings for load and robustness testing. Authored by a language model, with its distractors now including 65 real product strings taken from a Libyan commodity bulletin, and adversarially reviewed by a second one; NOT reviewed by a native speaker. Its realism is asserted rather than measured, so a figure produced against it is not a figure produced against a market.

_review: Known limitations, from the adversarial review. (1) These are CATEGORY codes carrying SKU phrasings: entries naming a plainly different product were deleted, but pack, carton and dozen wordings remain filed against single-unit codes, and a matcher scoring well on those would be conflating price points a price monitor exists to keep apart. (2) Recall-only: every line is a labelled positive, there are no distractors belonging to no catalogue item, so precision cannot be measured here. (3) The distribution is flat at roughly 30 per product; real reporter traffic is Zipfian. (4) A dozen entries are single bare nouns that are genuinely unanswerable from the string alone. (5) No Arabizi / franco-arabe, which is how a large share of people actually type. (6) Some brands could not be verified against a real shelf.
distractors: شكرا يا اخي الله يعطيك العافيه
_verification: Reviewed wording by wording against web sources by a research agent working from a Libyan-dialect brief. 39 entries were deleted as non-Libyan (Egyptian, Tunisian, Levantine or Gulf register, or brands with no Libyan market presence) and 35 were corrected. Every surviving wording carries a region tag in `regions`: west, east or both. A native Libyan speaker then corrected the review itself: free-range poultry and eggs are وطني, not عربي (the agent had corrected the Egyptian بلدي to another wrong word); a gas cylinder is اسطوانة / بمبلة / بومبة, never قارورة, which in Libya is a bottle; and a wallet is جزدان or تزدان, so محفظة was not the Libyan word for that either — it simply is not Libyan. Those corrections are applied. The corpus has still had only a partial native review, not a line-by-line one.

_open_questions: drinking_water_7l — RESOLVED on size and container word, still held on phrasing. A native speaker confirmed 2026-08-19 that the Libyan household jug is 7 litres and that 20L is not sold here; the item was re-specified from drinking_water_20l accordingly, and its reference price set to the 3 LYD Libya Al-Ahrar reported for a بانقة in April 2026. Eight wordings asserting ٢٠ لتر or 20L were removed because they described a container that does not exist. Of what remains, only بانقة is attested to a source; the brand and size phrasings around it are still model-generated, which is why this stays on hold. Venezuela keeps drinking_water_20l — the garrafón really is 20 litres there.

بيض عربي: Tripoli price bulletins carry البيض العربي as a distinct HIGHER-priced grade (28 د.ل) next to البيض العادي (16 د.ل). Given the ruling that free-range is وطني, is عربي nonetheless a real egg grade a reporter would type?
Sanitary pads: not one wording in the item could be attested to a Libyan source. Which of اولويز / كوتكس / مولبد / بيلا / نانا / سليبي are actually on Libyan shelves?
طهي vs طبخ: three Benghazi gas ads write طهي where western wordings say طبخ. Is that a real east/west split?

دحي spellings: only 'دحي' and 'طبق دحي' were observed in the wild. The other دحي rows were built by taking frames already attested in this item (طبق X، X ٣٠ حبة، X وطني) and swapping the head word in. Please prune any that a Libyan would not write — particularly دحية، الدحي، دحي عادي، and the Arabizi rows.
Does دحي take طبق the way بيض does, or is the tray called something else?
بيض is kept because Libyan price bulletins print it (البيض العادي، طبق البيض) — but it is now demoted below دحي in the sampling weights. Is that the right balance, or should بيض be cut back further?

كراسة vs دفتر — a 7x price difference hiding behind two words the catalogue treats as synonyms. school_notebook_80p lists both. On Libyan stationery pages in August 2026, دفتر 80 ورقة sells 5 for 1 dinar (0.20 each) at two independent shops, while a كراسة 60 ورقة is 1.25 and قرطاسية ماتا markets a كراسة 80 ورقة دبل غلاف as a premium line. So دفتر appears to be the cheap stapled exercise book and كراسة the bound one — but the same pages also use دفتر for sketchbooks and 180-sheet ledgers, so the split is not clean. Until it is settled the reference price of 2.30 is a price for an unspecified object. Ask a native speaker which word names the book a primary schoolchild is required to buy.

drinking_water_7l — HOLD LIFTED 2026-08-20. The hold said only بانقة itself was attested and the size and container phrasings around it were model-generated. Libyan Facebook now attests them verbatim: "بانقة مياه 7 لتر وصل سعرها اليوم في المنطقه الغربيه إلى 5 دينار", "بانقة المية بدت ب4", "بانقة الماء ٥ ديناااار", and a western-region marketers group naming the brands دجلة، النبع، الصافية. The 4.00 reference is corroborated by several independent posts; 5 in the west and 3.5 wholesale bracket it. Also learned: الاستيكة is the shrink-wrapped multipack (6 dinar at one Gharyan shop, 0.50 per قنينة), which is a different price point from the بانقة and must not be conflated with it.

harissa_can — still only 3 wordings after a targeted sweep, and that is a finding rather than a gap in effort. Libyan grocery pages barely advertise هريسة: searches for it return cooking shows, not price posts. The two brands that did surface (سيكام, and a "هريسة تونسية علبة ص") suggest it is sold as an everyday staple nobody markets. It is basketed, so its wordings matter; they will have to come from a reporter or a shelf photograph, not from search.

_measured_confusions._resolved_by_catalogue_coverage: زيت زيتون (olive oil, matched cooking_oil_1l at 0.727) and طماطم معجون (tomato paste, matched tomatoes_1kg at 0.739) are no longer confusions. They were never scoring failures — the catalogue had no entry for what the reporter typed, so 'nearest' was the wrong question. olive_oil_1l and tomato_paste_400g were added on 2026-08-15, catalogued but not basketed, and both now resolve to themselves at 0.990 through the exact-match short-circuit. Their wordings moved from distractors to items. زيتون اخضر مكبوس (pickled olives) and معجون سنسوداين (Sensodyne toothpaste) stay distractors: they share a token with the new items but are different products, and both still go to review rather than auto-resolve.
_measured_confusions._catalogue_coverage_2026_08_15: Nine items were added on 2026-08-15 — olive_oil_1l, tomato_paste_400g, canned_tuna_185g, pasta_500g, uht_milk_1l, couscous_1kg, sugar_1kg, harissa_can, bakery_flour_50kg — and 46 wordings moved out of distractors into them. All 46 now resolve correctly and auto-resolve at 0.990. The 164 distractors that remain are genuinely out of scope: greetings, test messages, cars, gold, phone credit, taxi fares, cement. Zero of them auto-resolve. Deliberately NOT catalogued despite looking like families: cheese (block cheddar, mozzarella, slices and triangles are different SKUs at different prices), yoghurt (زبادي and لبن are different products), chicken parts (breast, thigh and liver were flagged by the corpus review as exactly the distinction a price index must preserve), and tea (green and black).

_promoted.why: These wordings are now catalogue variants in countries/ly.yaml, so the matcher knows them. That is the point — a held-out split measured +19.1 points of top-1 on wordings it had never seen — but it has a cost that must not be forgotten: a matching score computed against the promoted part of this corpus is now measuring memorisation, not generalisation. The three held-back items still carry open questions and remain a clean test set, as does any real market data.
